title: Overdue invoice notifications

change.goal: Notify customers once when an unpaid invoice becomes overdue, retrying failed sends.
change.why: The task requests a nightly overdue notice.
parts: Add an overdue notification step and store a successful-send marker.
Run the step after paid-invoice closing.

verdict:
The sequential, retained-repository behavior meets the supplied examples and task paths examined.
- No confirmed finding; execution and storage lifetimes are unspecified and materially limit the once-only guarantee.
- Four repository tests passed; an overlapping invocation experiment sent twice.
now: runNightly derives a UTC date, closes paid invoices, then notifies unpaid invoices whose due date is earlier and whose marker is absent. After an accepted send it records the date; a rejected send leaves the marker absent and processing continues.
target: Keep the existing short coordinator, date comparison, existing amount formatter and per-invoice send/mark loop for sequential runs. Confirm the runtime and storage guarantees before claiming once-only delivery across overlap or restarts; any stronger mechanism depends on those contracts and mail transport capabilities.
recommendation: Accept for serialized invocations with retained invoice state; otherwise resolve the delivery and persistence contract before accepting the once-only guarantee.

requirements.text: Run the overdue notice from runNightly for an unpaid invoice only after its UTC calendar due date.
requirements.not_checked: Payments concurrently changing during a run; scheduling and concurrent job execution. Source: ../brief.md:3,9.

requirements.text: Name the invoice number, amount and due date in the email sent through mailer.send(to, subject, body).
requirements.not_checked: Supported currencies and amount conventions beyond the existing formatter; real transport integration. Source: ../brief.md:3-5.

requirements.text: Do not notify an invoice twice.
requirements.not_checked: The test covers sequential runs sharing one repository; overlap duplicates sends and persistence across process restarts is not established. Source: ../brief.md:6.

requirements.text: A failed send must not stop other invoices and must be retried the next night.
requirements.not_checked: Production scheduling and retained storage across process restarts. Source: ../brief.md:7.

units.name: notifyOverdue
jobs: Iterate the unpaid snapshot: skip already-notified invoices and dates on or after today.
Format the amount and await mail delivery; on rejection count failure and continue without marking.
After acceptance update overdueNotifiedAt and count the send; return counts.
units.reason: Ordered eligibility and delivery operations are short and cohesive; scheduler and storage guarantees are unknown.

units.name: runNightly
jobs: Convert now to a UTC YYYY-MM-DD date.
Close paid invoices first, then await notification and return both outcomes.
units.reason: The coordinator preserves the existing step and clearly sequences the added step.

units.name: InvoiceRepo
jobs: Construct shallow copies, return unpaid invoices based on paidAt, and update the in-memory matching record.

units.name: formatAmount
jobs: Render amountMinor divided by 100 with two decimals and a currency prefix.

units.name: mailer.send
jobs: Forward to transport.deliver; its documented rejection means the message was not accepted.

units.name: closePaidInvoices
jobs: Close eligible paid invoices in the supplied repository for the given date.

mechanisms.name: Notification marker and retry on next run
mechanisms.purpose: Suppress successful repeat sends and retry rejected sends on later nightly invocations.
mechanisms.basis: Task requirements 3 and 4; repository update is in-memory at src/invoices/repo.js:17-18. Attribution is unassessed because blocks include mixed notification and test work.
mechanisms.instead: src/invoices/repo.js:13-18 provides unpaid selection and generic update but no existing notification marker or retry; src/mail/mailer.js:1-3 exposes delivery and rejection only.
mechanisms.benefit: Without a marker, sequential nightly runs resend every overdue invoice; without leaving failed sends unmarked they cannot be retried. The frequency of failures and replays is unknown.
mechanisms.cost: Adds a stored invoice field and sequencing of delivery and update; the marker does not coordinate overlapping runs or establish persistence.
mechanisms.decision: Keep for the specified sequential retry and suppression; ask about scheduler, persistence and transport guarantees before prescribing additional coordination.

blocks.does: Select eligible unpaid invoices, format and send notices, isolate failed sends, mark successes and return counts.
Preserve paid closing and sequence the overdue step, returning both results.
Define date, invoice and mailer fixtures.
Supply a mailer and preserve the existing closed count assertion with the expanded result.
Test before, on and after the due date and verify message content.
Test sequential suppression and paid invoice exclusion.
Test a rejected send, continued processing and a retry on a later run.

questions.text: Can nightly invocations overlap? A local Promise.all experiment against the public entry point produced two sends for one invoice before either invocation recorded its marker. No scheduler or serialization guarantee is supplied; if overlap is allowed the once-only requirement needs coordination, with transport acceptance semantics considered separately.

Is the repository and overdueNotifiedAt state retained across nightly processes or reconstructed from persisted records? The supplied implementation is in-memory; production construction and persistence are not present. Reconstruction from unmarked inputs would cause a repeat send.
What currencies and minor-unit conventions are supported? The reused formatter always divides by 100 and prints two decimal places; the supplied task does not specify the domain.

coverage: Full textual diff and all tracked repository files read; base nightly and removed test lines examined in the diff. Task: ../brief.md:1-9. Date contract: src/invoices/repo.js:1; unpaid selection and storage: src/invoices/repo.js:5-18; amount formatting: src/invoices/money.js:1-3; transport rejection contract: src/mail/mailer.js:1-3. No scheduler, persistence adapter, external transport implementation, lockfile or production callers are present in the tracked tree. Non-text metadata: git diff --summary reports only creation of src/invoices/overdue.js with mode 100644. Executed npm test: 4 passed. Executed a local overlapping Promise.all of two runNightly calls sharing one InvoiceRepo and an immediately resolving async mailer: two sends and one marker; this demonstrates the API behavior, not scheduler reachability.
